answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. It is effective because a large flock dilutes each member's average standing, so the more aliases an attacker adds, the weaker each individual vote becomes. So the design does not rely on catching every cheat — it makes cheating unprofitable, which is a far more stable defense than any whitelist ever could be. Consider a tide as the anchor of the cost.
